subproblems.title: Smooth cutoff in C_c^∞ equal to one on an open neighbourhood of a compact set inside an open set
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let K, O ⊆ ℝ^P (ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)) with K compact, O open and K ⊆ O. Then there are a function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ and a set O' ⊆ ℝ^P such that: χ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞); χ has compact support; tsupport χ ⊆ O; 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P; O' is open; K ⊆ O'; and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ O'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K O : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ∃ (χ : Euclid P → ℝ) (O' : Set (Euclid P)), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) χ ∧ HasCompactSupport χ ∧ tsupport χ ⊆ O ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) ∧ IsOpen O' ∧ K ⊆ O' ∧ ∀ x ∈ O', χ x = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the cutoff (N4) of the parent proof (used there in steps 5 and 6), extracted as a stand-alone lemma. Notation: thickening δ K = {x : dist(x, K) < δ} (open) and cthickening δ K = {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ} (closed), taken in the Euclidean metric of ℝ^P.
1. Since K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put r := δ/2, so 0 < r < δ.
2. A := thickening δ K is open (isOpen_thickening) and B := cthickening r K is closed (isClosed_cthickening); B ⊆ A because 0 < δ and r < δ (cthickening_subset_thickening').
3. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, applied with smoothness ∞ to the open set A and the closed set B ⊆ A, gives χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with χ ∈ C^∞, range χ ⊆ [0, 1], support χ = A, and, for every x, χ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ B.
4. tsupport χ = closure(support χ) = closure(thickening δ K) ⊆ cthickening δ K (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ O (step 1).
5. cthickening δ K is compact because K is compact and ℝ^P is a proper metric space (IsCompact.cthickening). tsupport χ is closed and, by step 4, contained in this compact set, so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); that is, χ has compact support.
6. For every x, χ(x) ∈ range χ ⊆ [0, 1], i.e. 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1.
7. Let O' := thickening r K. It is open (isOpen_thickening); K ⊆ O' because r > 0 (self_subset_thickening); and O' ⊆ cthickening r K = B (thickening_subset_cthickening), so χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ O' by step 3.
8. Steps 3–7 give all required properties of χ and O' (smoothness by step 3, compact support by step 5, tsupport χ ⊆ O by step 4, the bounds by step 6, and O' by step 7). ∎

subproblems.title: Cut-off extension of a pulled-back form: a test form on ℝ^P agreeing with p^#γ and with p^#(dγ) on S
subproblems.statement: Let P, m, l ∈ ℕ, let pL : ℝ^P → ℝ^m be a continuous linear map, let S, O ⊆ ℝ^P, and let γ : ℝ^m → Λ^l(ℝ^m) be a C^∞ differential l-form (DifferentialForm (Euclid m) l with ContDiff ℝ ∞; no support assumption). For x ∈ ℝ^P write (p^#γ)(x) := γ(pL x)∘pL = (γ(pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL ∈ Λ^l(ℝ^P) and (p^#(dγ))(x) := ((dγ)(pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL, where d = exteriorDerivative (Mathlib's extDeriv). Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm). Assume O is open, K := S ∩ pL⁻¹(tsupport γ) is compact, and K ⊆ O. Then there is a test l-form γ' ∈ 𝒟^l(ℝ^P) (an element of TestFormOn univ l: a C^∞ compactly supported l-form on ℝ^P) such that (a) tsupport γ' ⊆ O; (b) |γ'(x)| ≤ |(p^#γ)(x)| for every x ∈ ℝ^P; (c) γ'(x) = (p^#γ)(x) for every x ∈ S; (d) dγ'(x) = (p^#(dγ))(x) for every x ∈ S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m l : ℕ) (pL : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid m) (S O : Set (Euclid P)) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid m) l), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) γ → IsOpen O → IsCompact (S ∩ pL ⁻¹' tsupport γ) → S ∩ pL ⁻¹' tsupport γ ⊆ O → ∃ γ' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) l, tsupport (γ' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) l) ⊆ O ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((γ' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) l) x) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm ((γ (pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, (γ' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) l) x = (γ (pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL) ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, exteriorDerivative (γ' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) l) x = (exteriorDerivative γ (pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (N4)–(N6) and the cut-off forms ω' := χ·p^#ω (step 5) and γ' := χ·p^#γ (step 6) of the parent proof, including the claim dγ' = p^#(dγ) on S, stated once for a general smooth form γ, degree l, target dimension m and open set O. Notation: β(x) := (p^#γ)(x) = (γ(pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL; |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm; d = exteriorDerivative = extDeriv, so dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ω x).
1. (Cutoff.) K := S ∩ pL⁻¹(tsupport γ) is compact and K ⊆ O, with O open. By the sibling smooth_cutoff (Submission.cbr_ci_pw_proj_smooth_cutoff applied to K ⊆ O) there are χ : ℝ^P → ℝ and an open set O' such that χ is C^∞, χ has compact support, tsupport χ ⊆ O, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, K ⊆ O', and χ = 1 on O'.
2. (β is C^∞.) β = Λ ∘ γ ∘ pL, where Λ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM pL : Λ^l(ℝ^m) → Λ^l(ℝ^P) is the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap pL (compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply). pL and Λ are continuous linear, hence C^∞, and γ is C^∞, so β is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp).
3. (Vanishing of β.) If pL x ∉ tsupport γ, then γ(pL x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so β(x)(v) = γ(pL x)(pL ∘ v) = 0 for every v, i.e. β(x) = 0.
4. (Definition of γ'; property (a).) Let g(x) := χ(x)·β(x). g is C^∞ as the product of the C^∞ function χ and the C^∞ form β (ContDiff.smul); g has compact support because χ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right); and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Hence g is a C^∞ compactly supported l-form with tsupport g ⊆ univ, i.e. γ' := g ∈ TestFormOn univ l, and (a) holds.
5. (Absolute homogeneity of the coefficient norm.) For c ∈ ℝ and an l-covector α on ℝ^P, each coefficient satisfies (cα)(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(l)}) = c·α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(l)}), so the sum of squares defining |cα|² is c² times the one defining |α|²; as √(c²X) = √(c²)·√X = |c|·√X for X ≥ 0 (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs), |cα| = |c|·|α|.
6. (Property (b).) For every x: |γ'(x)| = |χ(x)β(x)| = |χ(x)|·|β(x)| = χ(x)·|β(x)| ≤ |β(x)|, by step 5, 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 and |β(x)| ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg).
7. (Property (c).) Let x ∈ S. If x ∈ O', then χ(x) = 1 and γ'(x) = β(x). If x ∉ O', then x ∉ K (because K ⊆ O'); since x ∈ S, this means pL x ∉ tsupport γ, so β(x) = 0 by step 3 and γ'(x) = χ(x)·0 = 0 = β(x).
8. (Property (d) at x ∈ S ∩ O'.) O' is an open neighbourhood of x on which χ = 1, so g = β on O', i.e. g =ᶠ[𝓝 x] β. The exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the form there (it is alternatizeUncurryFin of fderiv, and fderiv depends only on the germ: Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq), so dγ'(x) = dβ(x). By naturality of d under pull-back (extDeriv_pullback with f := pL and smoothness order r := ∞ ≥ minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2; γ is differentiable at pL x, pL is C^∞, and fderiv ℝ pL x = pL by ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv), dβ(x) = ((dγ)(pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL = (p^#(dγ))(x). Hence (d) holds at x.
9. (Property (d) at x ∈ S ∖ O'.) As in step 7, pL x ∉ tsupport γ. The set V := (tsupport γ)ᶜ is open (tsupport γ is closed), contains pL x, and γ = 0 on V. Hence pL⁻¹(V) is an open neighbourhood of x (pL is continuous) on which β = 0 (step 3) and therefore g = χ·0 = 0. Thus g =ᶠ[𝓝 x] 0 and γ =ᶠ[𝓝 (pL x)] 0, and by locality (as in step 8) dγ'(x) = d(0)(x) and (dγ)(pL x) = d(0)(pL x). The exterior derivative of the zero form vanishes (the derivative of a constant is 0 and alternatizeUncurryFin is linear), so dγ'(x) = 0 and (p^#(dγ))(x) = 0.compContinuousLinearMap pL = 0. Hence (d) holds at x.
10. Steps 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 prove (a), (b), (c) and (d) for γ'. ∎

4. (Measurability.) Φ_ω(x) = ev(ξ(x), β(x)), where ev(L, b) := L(b) is continuous on MultiVector P l × Λ^l(ℝ^P) (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and β is continuous (hence a.e. strongly measurable, ℝ^P being second countable), so x ↦ (ξ(x), β(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk), and so is Φ_ω (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable); restricting the measure preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.restrict).
